name: Continuous Shot. The label was normalized from an explicit request for one continuous shot. Category: Motion Design and Cinematography.
visualIdentity: Explicitly defined by one readable camera path through continuous space that preserves subjects, lighting, and occlusion. Structure comes from internal action, scale changes, or transformations, with deliberate acceleration and pauses. Unexplained resets, wall intersections, and hidden discontinuities must be avoided. Materials and typography are unspecified.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to any single unbroken camera journey. Listed good fits are psychedelic and demoscene imagery, infinite zoom and kaleidoscopic transitions, and surreal or abstract spatial passages. Company tours and process walkthroughs are only inferred suitable through the diorama hybrid, not stated as direct uses.
limitations: Adapt or omit when the viewer must read dense text during travel. Omit when a one-shot requirement would be broken by an unplanned hidden reset. Omit when the topic or style needs stable orientation or reduced motion. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics.
palette: The source gives no fixed palette for this style. An optional, reference-dependent example uses background #F2EBDD, foreground #343E43, and accent_1 #8D957D, with gradients disabled. Foreground on background measures 9.239:1, while accent_1 behind foreground text measures 3.511:1, so accent_1 is decorative only. Exact task or brand colors override these values, and assets must not be recolored. Color families and color count limits are unspecified.
motionAndInteraction: Camera pose must be computed directly from time, with cached simulation so seeking cannot change results. Verify direct, backward, and sequential seeks plus loop seams. Scroll input is optional and belongs only to interactive delivery, not video export. Optional motion references are conditional: motion-002 (vortex passage) only for a meaningful chapter, motion-010 (full orbit) only with complete geometry or turntable views, motion-015 for narrative steps, and motion-019 only with real depth or an identified 2.5D approximation. Reduced-motion alternatives are unspecified.
audio: The source specifies no audio for this style and imposes no fixed genre, tempo, instrument, voice, or mandatory layer. Audio should be proposed from topic, audience, storyboard, and motion cadence. Music, voiceover, sung vocals, effects, ambience, or silence are all options. Speech must stay intelligible, avoid clipping, and not compete with narration. Any motion-010 or motion-002 accent is optional.
assetRequirements: Assets and exact copy are unspecified in the source. Prepare and load fonts and assets before rendering, seed randomness, and cache stateful simulations. Motion-010 requires a complete modeled subject or sufficient captured turntable views, because a single flat sprite cannot reveal unseen sides. Motion-019 requires real depth geometry or a clearly identified 2.5D approximation, not a flat image scaled as a dolly.
combinations: Continuous Shot alone suits any single unbroken camera journey. A suggested hybrid places style-079 diorama rooms as a bounded environment with uniform scale and one camera spline, plus style-093 spatial typography framed frontally for reading holds. Three.js remains the single renderer. Avoid camera passing through walls and overdetailed sets. Hybrid application is suggested by the source, not verified.
productionApproach: HyperFrames is the primary pipeline for composition, timing, audio sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. Three.js is the style renderer for geometry, camera, materials, and lighting. GSAP is the motion engine, using one paused, seekable timeline with one owner per property. chroma.js is optional for palette validation and contrast. Inspect key frames, watch the full video, and verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio sync, and loop continuity.
